hints: Only one section changes. Which node stays fixed just before the section, and could you grow the reversed part one node at a time?

In-place reversal of a sublist with a dummy head. Walk to before (the node at position lo−1). Then, hi − lo times, take the node right after the current stretch start and move it to the front of the stretch.

1. Make dummy pointing to head; walk before lo−1 steps from dummy.
  2. Let start = before.next (it will end up at the end of the stretch).
  3. Repeat hi−lo times: move = start.next; start.next = move.next; move.next = before.next; before.next = move.
  4. Return dummy.next.

approaches.name: Copy values
approaches.idea: Copy the stretch's values into an array, reverse it, and write them back.

approaches.name: Optimal: front-insertion in place
approaches.idea: One pass to the start, then relink each node of the stretch to the front.

explain: For 1→2→3→4→5→6 with lo = 2, hi = 5: before is 1 and start is 2. Moving 3 to the front gives 1→3→2→4…, then 4 gives 1→4→3→2→5…, then 5 gives 1→5→4→3→2→6. The invariant: after each move, before.next is the head of the reversed part and start is its tail, still linked to the untouched rest. The dummy node handles lo = 1, and lo = hi simply does zero moves.
recognize: Reverse only part of a linked list between two positions → anchor the node before the part and reverse in place.
javascript: function reverseBetween(head, lo, hi) { const a = []; for (let c = head; c; c = c.next) a.push(c.val); const m = a.slice(lo-1, hi).reverse(); a.splice(lo-1, hi-lo+1, ...m); let c = head; for (const v of a) { c.val = v; c = c.next; } return head; }
